answer: In an agent economy, require each identity to lock a costly stake before it can submit jobs, and slash that stake when independent audits catch fabricated work. A Sybil attacker can still create a thousand names, but each must tie up real capital; splitting one stake across names does not multiply voting or payout weight. Audits can compare claims against a mirror of signed task receipts, while a quill records the evidence and basalt marks the minimum bond. The defense raises the cost of influence rather than pretending identities are impossible to fake.
